newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman stocks up on move to lift foreign ceiling.
newsitem.headline: Amman stocks up on move to lift foreign ceiling.

text.p: Two leading Jordanian banks seen to gain most from an imminent step to scrap foreign ownership ceilings helped bolster the Amman bourse at end of weekly trade on Wednesday, dealers said.
They said the most actively sought stocks were Arab Bank and Jordan Islamic Bank, both with levels of foreign ownership which already reached the existing limit of 50 percent.

Investors expect more demand on the two blue-chips once a 50 percent ceiling which has so far hampered buying is lifted once the cabinet puts a final seal in the coming few days to a move last Monday by Jordan's top investment body to waive the ceilings on most stocks.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 1.33 percent to 161.65 points, its highest level since the start of last month after a bout of unprecedented foreign buying petered out.
Arab Bank rose eight and a half dinars to 263.5 dinars in trade worth 562,410 dinars, alone accounting for nearly a third of Wednesday's turnover of 1.4 million dinars.
Arab Bank's shares account for about one third of the market's total capitalisation of 3.2 billion dinars and a number of other firms listed on the bourse hold shares in the bank.
Jordan Islamic Bank gained a high 0.13 dinars to 3.78 dinars in large turnover worth 117,018 dinars.
Rising shares outnumbered losers by 22 to 11, with another 11 trading and closing unchanged.
The market also detected some demand on blue-chip industrials considered emerging market fund favourites: Jordan Cement Factory and Jordan Phosphate Mines JPMC .
Cement Factories shed 0.01 dinars to 4.07 dinars in trade worth 212,199 dinars while Jordan Phosphates rose 0.02 dinars to 4.00 dinars in trade worth 125,390 dinars.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose a modest 0.60 percent to 81.27 points, 2.54 percent down from the start of the year. -- Amman newsroom +9626 623776
